notes: Closure is a short interactive procedure, not a button (questionnaire 3.11). Sizes come from the Cardiac Interventions Today device guide; steps and failure modes from the ACC Coronary Interventions Handbook chapter. Steps marked 'to source' need the instructions for use before the device gets an interactive sequence.

items.genericName: Anchor, collagen and suture closure device

mechanism.text: Suture, collagen and anchor sandwich of the arteriotomy

deviceSheath.note: Dedicated sheath with an arteriotomy locator.

steps.text: Remove the procedure sheath and place the dedicated 6F or 8F sheath with arteriotomy locator.
Advance it 1 cm into the lumen beyond the point where blood stops flowing from the drip hole.
Deploy the anchor and pull it back against the arterial wall.
Seat the collagen plug just outside the arterial wall and tamp it with the tamping tube.

reaccess.text: Re-access at the same site before 90 days should be 1 cm proximal to the previous puncture.

failureModes.text: Incomplete anchor apposition against the lumen: hemostasis fails.
Collagen plug ends up intravascular: limb ischemia.
Ineffective after a posterior-wall puncture or in an irregular, diseased lumen.
Do not trim a plug that shows at the skin entry.

steps.text: Advance the device over the wire until blood return shows.
Pull lever 1 to deploy the anchor inside the lumen.
Depress plunger 2 to send two needles to the anchor, creating a suture loop.
Advance the pre-tied knot with the knot pusher, then cut the suture.

largeBore.text: For sheaths 5 to 8F a single device is deployed at the end of the procedure.
For sheaths above 8F, pre-close with two devices before upsizing: the first at 10 o'clock, the second at 2 o'clock, crossing the sutures over the arteriotomy.

failureModes.text: Complications are more likely with peripheral arterial disease, in women and in vessels under 5 mm.
Calcification deflects the needles and the device fails.
In obese patients the fascia can be mistaken for the vessel wall; a knot secured there bleeds.
A bifurcation within reach of the anchor can tether the back wall and occlude the femoral artery.

steps.text: Deployment steps to source from the instructions for use.
Fill the small semicompliant balloon with contrast, inflate it inside the artery and pull it back against the arteriotomy.
Advance the shuttle to bring the PEG plug to the artery, then advance the plug toward the arteriotomy.
After 30 s, lay the device flat for another 90 s of curing.

failureModes.text: Over-advancing the delivery system can push sealant into the lumen.
failureModes.note: From the research notes; confirm against the instructions for use.

veinSheath.note: Inner diameter; up to 15F outer diameter.

deviceSize.note: For 10 to 20F devices (12 to 25F outer diameter).

uses.text: Large-bore femoral arterial access such as EVAR
uses.note: Follows from its 10-20F sizing; confirm with an IR reviewer.

items.brandName: Radial compression band (e.g., TR Band, Zephyr)

mechanism.text: External compression with an air-filled bladder

steps.text: Inflate the band to about 18 mL.
Deflate until a small amount of bleeding shows, then re-inject about 2 mL of air (patent hemostasis).
Leave it inflated about 45 minutes, then deflate about 3 mL every 5 minutes.

mechanism.text: Pressure over the arteriotomy against the femoral head

duration.text: Durations by sheath size and ACT still to source

rules.text: Femoral closure devices assume an anterior common femoral puncture above the bifurcation; atheroma, dissection and significant calcification are relative contraindications.
After uneventful access and closure, patients may walk within 2 hours.
Mynx is used only for sheaths up to 7F.
